passage:
A small store in Hill Village sells used books, cups, bags, and toys. There are no price tags. Instead, a sign says, "Pay what you think is fair."
Some visitors are confused. They ask the owner how much things cost. The owner always says, "Think about the item, your money, and the next customer."
Most people pay carefully. Some pay more than expected. A few pay very little, but the owner does not stop them.
The store uses the money to help old people in the village buy food. Because of this, many villagers bring things they no longer need.
The store is not only selling objects. It is testing whether people can be honest when no one gives them an exact number.
